title: Timed Biology practice 2 with mark scheme
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y11 lesson 123 (Timed Biology practice 2 with mark scheme (portal))
intro: Test. Answer every question in the spaces provided. Show your working: marks are given for method. The marks for each question are shown in brackets.

questions.q: 'Calculate' answers lose marks most often because...
questions.a: A) The equation is not written. Writing the equation and substitution earns method marks even if the final answer is wrong.

questions.q: Which feature is typical of a wind-pollinated flower?
questions.a: B) Feathery stigma outside the flower. A large feathery stigma catches pollen blown in the air.

questions.q: Cross Bb × bb. Probability of bb?
questions.a: B) 50%. Offspring: Bb, Bb, bb, bb, so 2/4 = 50%.

questions.q: Why does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: It provides a pathway with lower activation energy
questions.a: B) It provides a pathway with lower activation energy. More collisions now exceed the lower activation energy.

questions.q: A gas at 200 kPa in 3.0 L is compressed to 1.5 L at constant temperature. New pressure?
questions.a: C) 400 kPa. p₁V₁ = p₂V₂: 200 × 3.0 = p₂ × 1.5, so p₂ = 400 kPa.

questions.q: Why do resistant bacteria increase?
options: Non-resistant bacteria are killed, resistant ones survive and reproduce
questions.a: B) Non-resistant bacteria are killed, resistant ones survive and reproduce. The antibiotic is the selection pressure; it does not cause the mutation.

questions.q: Mock repair task on the portal: pick your 3 lowest-scoring questions (one from each paper), rewrite each answer to the mark scheme in green, then name the error type.
questions.a: Pupils' own corrected answers with error types
questions.model: Teacher repairs one 6-mark answer on screen against the mark scheme, ticking each creditworthy point.

questions.q: Write your six-week repair plan in the portal response box: topic, lesson where it is revised, practice set. Starter: 'My costliest topic is...'
questions.a: Pupils' own plan linked to lessons 107 to 131

questions.q: Calculate your mock percentage for each paper and the marks needed for your target grade.
questions.a: Pupils' own calculation

questions.q: Mock answer: 'v = 12' for v = fλ with f = 4 Hz, λ = 3 m. Rewrite for full marks.
questions.model: Write the equation. Substitute with units. Give the answer with its unit: 12 m/s. The unit was missing.

questions.q: Rewrite 'osmosis is water moving' for 3 marks.
questions.a: Net movement of water molecules (1) across a partially permeable membrane (1) from a dilute to a more concentrated solution (1)

questions.q: Which command word needs a judgement?
questions.a: Evaluate

questions.q: Plan an investigation to show that seeds need water to germinate. Portal response box.
questions.a: Two sets of the same seeds (1), same number and type (1); one with damp cotton wool, one dry (1); same temperature and oxygen/light (1); leave several days (1); count the number germinated and compare / calculate % (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes the first point: 'Place 20 cress seeds on damp cotton wool and 20 on dry cotton wool.'

questions.q: Describe how a pollen grain from one flower leads to a seed in another.
questions.a: Pollen carried by insect/wind to the stigma (1); pollen tube grows down the style (1) to the ovule (1); male nucleus fuses with female nucleus/fertilisation (1)

questions.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of cuttings for a farmer.
questions.a: Advantage: quick, identical desired features (1); disadvantage: no variation, all vulnerable to the same disease (1)

questions.q: Explain why offspring from asexual reproduction are identical.
questions.a: Only one parent (1); cells divide by mitosis so genetic material is copied exactly (1)
questions.model: One parent, no fusion of gametes. Mitosis copies DNA exactly. So offspring are genetically identical.

questions.q: State what happens to the ovule and ovary after fertilisation.
questions.a: Ovule becomes the seed (1); ovary becomes the fruit (1)

questions.q: Give two adaptations of wind-pollinated anthers and pollen.
questions.a: Anthers hang outside the flower; pollen is light and produced in large amounts

questions.q: Pedigree on the sheet (two unaffected parents, one affected son). (a) Is the allele dominant or recessive? Explain [2]. (b) Give the parents' genotypes [2]. (c) Draw a Punnett square for the next child and give the probability it is unaffected [3].
questions.a: (a) recessive (1): unaffected parents had an affected child, so both carry the allele (1); (b) both Aa (2); (c) AA, Aa, Aa, aa (2); 3/4 or 75% unaffected (1)

questions.q: Explain why most human features show a range of phenotypes.
questions.a: Most features are polygenic (1), controlled by several genes (1), and also affected by the environment (1)

questions.q: Two tall plants give 75 tall and 25 dwarf offspring. What were the parents' genotypes? Explain.
questions.a: Both Tt (1): a 3:1 ratio shows both parents carry the recessive allele (1)

questions.q: Cystic fibrosis is recessive (f). Two carriers (Ff) have a child. Probability the child has CF?
questions.a: Gametes F, f from each (1); Punnett FF, Ff, Ff, ff (1); 1 in 4, 25% (1)
questions.model: Carriers are Ff. Each gives F or f. Square: FF, Ff, Ff, ff. Only ff has CF: 1 out of 4.

questions.q: Define phenotype.
questions.a: The observable characteristics
